name: HMS Prince of Wales

sources.title: HMS Prince of Wales (53) — King George V-class battleship; sunk on 10 December 1941; the wreck upside down at about 68 m off Kuantan, illegally salvaged in the 21st century, a Protected Place since 2001
UK Ministry of Defence — wreck assessment of HMS Prince of Wales and HMS Repulse (2019, FOI 20190/7097): intact shells and cordite scattered on the wreck sites
Pacific Wrecks — HMS Prince of Wales hull damage
The Star (2025) — Sunken ships and stolen history (looting of the wrecks)

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q724919_hms_prince_of_wales.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/dresskit.py) with AI assistance. Upside down at about 68 m, a little over to starboard, resting on her deck edge with the bridge, funnels and turrets crushed down into the bottom; the bilge, the four shafts and screws and the rudder uppermost; the hull stove in aft on the port side (torpedoes) and plates torn away by the scrap thieves; shells and cordite charges strewn about. A war grave (327 men). The angle, the heading (not published: 0), the torpedo damage and the extent of the looting are approximate. model_built.glb: the battleship as she sailed in 1941.
